title: I spent 18 months making a game during COVID, put it aside for years, and came back to finish it with AI
author: Master_Ad_939
selftext:
During COVID I started making a cozy 3D adventure. I began in Xcode, then switched to Godot. I was working alone and figuring most of it out as I went. After about a year and a half, I went back to work and couldn’t see how I was going to finish it on my own. So I put it aside for a few years.



A few months ago I picked it up again. This time I used Claude and ChatGPT to help with coding, debugging and testing, while I kept steering the story, the world and the look of the game. One example was the camera: it could feel awkward when I played as the cat and tried to reach a key under a cabinet. I could give the tools a specific problem to investigate and retest, then judge in the game whether the change actually felt better. I also used generative tools for some of the music and story cinematics. The video labels the cinematics separately from the gameplay.



The game is called The Last Lantern (Lantaarnlicht). You play a kid in a canal town that changes from Halloween to New Year’s. You can turn into a cat to squeeze under a stack of sail crates, or become a crow and fly out past the lighthouse. Along the way you get to know the neighbours and help bring light back to their streets.

I’ve submitted the game to Apple for App Store review. Hitting Submit after letting this project sit for years felt surreal. Now I’m just hoping it gets through review.

It’s a paid game for iPhone and iPad, with no ads or in-app purchases. I’m planning to launch at €4.99 for the first two weeks, then €6.99. what do you think of this price? Is it realistic?

I’d love an honest gut reaction to the gameplay in the trailer. What would you be most curious to try, and what looks rough or unclear? I’m also happy to talk about the early version and what AI helped with or got wrong.

![video](dkq2nj27c62i1 "The 52-second gameplay trailer, including a few story cinematics.")

I’ve included three then-and-now comparisons from the project. The panels on the left approximate how the town looked about 14 months into solo development during COVID. The panels on the right show the current build. The bakery street, the Christmas square and the canal route I used to test crow flight were already taking shape back then.

![img](vg10kamyf62i1 "Bakery street. The clock tower and shop are still there. The cobblestones, textured walls and street details came later.")

![img](usy0dbmyf62i1 "Christmas square. The gazebo and tree date back to the early build. The snowy roofs and winter lighting are from the current version.")

![img](6vbyiamyf62i1 "Flying as a crow. The old canal route is still there, with more foliage, detailed rooftops and a brighter canal in the current build.")

comments.body: Shapeshifting concept, there was just another game of shapeshifting someone else posted today. 4.99 might work. Let us know the results after the first week of release.
